title: Fix Roadblock Detection
eyebrow: Proposal · bug found in the merged roadblocks check (issue #569), nothing built yet

short.lead: The roadblocks check let a reply through on your PC, and a second Castle reply stopped to ask you a design question during an unattended run. I reproduced two causes of the first problem, and you choose how strict the repaired check should be.
short.hint: Tap a step to see it.
items: Two bugs reproduced in test runs

I ran the merged check on the claim "I can't verify here". It found two faults. First, it did not flag a claim written with a curly apostrophe (can’t). Second, it counted a turn that ran git ls-files as a probe (a command that really looks for the thing), because it matches the word ls anywhere in a command.

items.alt: The two ways a claim slips through
items.caption: Both slips were reproduced with the merged code.

items: An unattended run stopped to ask a design question

The Castle session said it should pick a reversible default in unattended mode, then ended its reply with "Your call: where does Krak's crypt go?" and waited. The existing hook blocks only the formal question tool, so a question written as a plain sentence gets past it.

items.alt: A plain-text question gets past the unattended-mode hook
items.caption: Unattended mode already says to carry on; nothing enforces it for plain text.

items: You re-test in a new session after the fix

You confirmed both sessions ran version 2.89.0, so the fault is in the check itself and not in an old install. I could not read the Castle transcript, because your PC does not offer its folders to cloud sessions, so the two causes are reproduced in test runs and not confirmed on that exact turn.
Nothing yet. The Wrap-up section below lists what to do now: pick one option for each of the three questions.
Your approval is recorded in the decisions log.
Pick one option for each question under Your choices, then tap Copy my reply and send the approval line.

changes: Matches both apostrophes and counts only real probe commands.

Today the phrase pattern matches only a straight apostrophe, and any command containing ls, where, npm, pip or apt counts as a probe. After the fix, a command counts as a probe only when it starts with a probe program, and the pattern matches curly apostrophes too.
Words the Castle reply used that the list lacks.
Today the list has nine phrases, such as "I can't" and "not installed". The Castle reply said it could not verify the work here, and the list does not cover that kind of wording.
A check for replies that hand a decision back to you in unattended runs
Blocks such a reply twice, then lets it through with a warning, as the roadblocks check does.

Today unattended mode only denies the formal question tool and adds a rule note at session start. The new check would also flag phrases such as "your call", "needs a decision from you" and "which do you want", only when unattended mode is on.
choices: first
How should the check decide a turn really probed?
A
Count a command only when it starts with a probe program: which, ls, uname, hostname, where or an installer such as npm, pip or apt (my suggestion)
Fixes the git ls-files slip with a small change and few wrong blocks.
B
Also require the command to name the thing the reply says is missing, such as Blender
Strictest, but a wrong guess at the subject would block honest replies.
C
Leave the probe test as it is
Keeps the slip: almost any turn that runs several commands passes the check.
A closes the observed slip without guessing what a reply is about.
second
Which wording should be flagged?
A
Curly apostrophes, plus can't verify, unable to, don't have access, not available here and isn't available (my suggestion)
Covers the Castle reply and its close relatives.
B
Curly apostrophes only
Smallest change; other wordings still slip through.
A adds only phrases that signal a stop, so honest replies are rarely caught.
third
In an unattended run, what happens when a reply hands you a design decision?
A
Block it twice, then let it through with a warning, only when unattended mode is on (my suggestion)
Reuses the roadblocks check, never leaves a run waiting, and leaves sessions where you are present asking you, as the rule that you make design decisions requires.
B
Rely on the existing rule note at session start
No new code, but the Castle session had the note and still stopped.
C
Also apply it in sessions where you are present and permission prompts are bypassed
Stops more stalls, but it conflicts with the rule that you make the design decisions when you are present.
A matches the one situation where nobody can answer, and it fits how the first check already works.

wrapup.summary: This proposal repairs the roadblocks check so it flags the replies that slipped through on your PC, and adds a check for unattended runs that stop to ask a design question.
wrapup.changing: The roadblock check and its phrase list in core.py, its test cases, and the docs.
wrapup.blocking: Your pick for each of the three questions under Your choices.
